notes.title: Corpse of Discovery Reduced Price!
notes.notes: Some experiences are polarizing, and we're OK with that.  Corpse of Discovery is unique experience, and not for everyone, but we are truly moved by some of the heartfelt reactions we've read in comments to the message we are trying to share in this game.  In the hopes of making it easier for the people that would enjoy this type of game to give it a try, we have reduced the price, and there are performance settings you can turn down for less powerful machines, found under Options in the main menu.

notes.title: 10/15 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Further optimized levels and content to address performance issues. Exposed more options for quality settings including grass density, ambient occlusion, fog, and updated depth of field. If you experience low fps, try turning some of these settings down.

Updates:
    - Ambient Occlusion, Fog, HUD lines, and Grass Density added to Settings Menu.
    - Detail Settings renamed to Quality Settings.
    - Updated Depth of Field settings.
    - Further optimized Swamp level - Tweaked LODs and collision generation.
    - Updated loading audio files to stream in more smoothly.
    - Multiple performance improvements in various levels.
   - Button to screenshot game and computer specs for better reporting of issues.

notes.title: 9/4 Patch Updates
notes.notes:
Made additional updates to address performance issues some users are having. Of note, we are still working on the memory leak some users are experiencing. If you have these issues, it would be a huge favor to us if you could share the specifics in the steam forums. 

•             PERF: Removed performance issue from Lava and Abstract
•             PERF: Re-enabled chunk combiner on planets. to reduce draw calls
•             Added waypoints to Hub interacts 
•             Changed some dialog to better explain unfolding events
•             Changed side mission waypoints to be more noticable.
•             Added  additional 'seeking creatures' to worlds.  
•             Changed order of some side side objectives.
•             fixed player walking past airlock door entrance. 
•             Readjusted audio balance in planets
•             Adjust how long sub objective text stays on screen.
•             Fix invert input to only flip Y Axis 
•             Fix bug where you fall out of 'bone cave' at start

notes.title: IMPORTANT NOTES
notes.notes:
-  THIS GAME ISN'T FOR EVERYONE. It is a "walking simulator", with an occasional jetpack and deadly obstacles. It also gets pretty strange and introspective. If this all sounds like it isn't the game for you, then it probably won't be.

-  We are very sorry some of you are having performance issues!  We haven't seen this in our testing, so we are trying to figure out the discrepancies. As soon as we do, we will release a patch, alongside other bug fixes!

-  There are different ways to interpret the ending of the game, and while not everyone will like the ending (just like most movies, opinions will differ), it's exactly what we were going for.

[i]If you feel unhappy and that you didn't know what kind of game you were getting into, please do ask Steam for a refund, we don't want anyone to be disappointed with their purchase![/i]

notes.title: Corpse of Discovery launches with a disturbing new trailer
notes.notes:
Corpse of Discovery was announced in July with an intriguing premise and a strangely creepy teaser. It's a loose sci-fi twist on the Corps of Discovery that existed briefly in the early 1800s, but instead of sending intrepid explorers into the American West, it sends them into deep space. The developer, Phosphor Games, didn't reveal a release date but said in the announcement that it was "coming soon," and they weren't kidding, because it's out now.

The launch trailer is similar to the teaser but reveals a little more about some of the pressures you'll face as a deep-space explorer torn between supporting his family and returning to them. And of course, what was supposed to be a routine job turns out to be anything but. "You wake up on a base in a new, unexplored planet. Your landing craft is torn to pieces and your gear is scattered," the Steam description states. "Why are you here? What is your mission? How will you ever get back home to your family?"

The game was actually released on the 25th, but the release didn't go live quite when it was supposed to and so I ended up putting this off, and then forgetting about it, until now. Sorry about that. The good news, for those interested, is that the launch promotion price of $13/ 10 is still in place, and will remain so until September 1.
